# Setting Up a Darkroom Pro Print Controller

OrderHub Desktop (OHD) sends jobs to Darkroom Pro by writing a small instruction file (a **.txt** file) into the folder that Darkroom Pro's Command folder watches. Darkroom Pro picks the file up, finds the images, and prints them on the size and paper named in the file.

This article covers:

- adding a Darkroom Pro controller;
- what every setting does;
- the **Page padding** option for white borders;
- setting up a second Darkroom Pro controller, so you can move a job onto a different printer.

![Darkroom Pro](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/aeaf7f39-b9d7-4b39-a320-c6c760512b9e.png)

---

## Before You Start

* Darkroom Pro must already be set up with your print sizes (for example **4x6**, **5x7**, **6x7**) and your paper names (for example **Lustre 1**). OHD writes these names into the file exactly as you type them, so they must match Darkroom Pro letter for letter.
* You need the location of Darkroom Pro's Command folder, and the OHD computer must be able to reach it.
* The instruction file tells Darkroom Pro where each image is, using OHD's download folder. If Darkroom Pro runs on a different computer, that computer must be able to open the images at the same path.

---

## Adding the Controller

1. In OHD, go to **Settings → Routing**.
2. In the **Order Controllers** section, click **+ Add Controller**. The **Add Controller** window opens.
3. In **Name**, type a name you'll recognise, for example **Darkroom – Printer 1**.
4. In **Type**, choose **Darkroom Pro**.
   * Note: a new controller opens as a Noritsu (DPOF) controller, so always change the **Type** first. The Darkroom Pro settings only appear once it is selected.
5. Next to **Output Path**, click **Browse...** and choose Darkroom Pro's Command folder.
6. Fill in the rest of the settings (explained below), then click **Save Controller**.

![Add Darkroom Pro Controller](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/9190e421-e065-468f-ac2b-e355efc1c7af.png)

Once saved, the controller appears as a card in **Order Controllers**, showing:

* **Output:**, followed by the Output Path;
* **Sizes:** and **Media:**, with your first few translations;
* the **Edit**, **Duplicate** and **Delete** buttons, and an **Auto Print** tick box.

* Note: deleting a controller also removes all of its **Process Routing** and **Channel Mappings** entries.

---

## The Settings

### Output Path

The folder Darkroom Pro watches for new orders (its Command folder). OHD writes the .txt instruction files here, and Darkroom Pro picks them up from this folder. This setting is required.

### Processed Folder Name

The sub-folder of the Output Path that Darkroom Pro moves an order's .txt file into once it has taken the order. Used with **Check Order Status**. Type the folder name, for example **Processed**.

### OrderLastName Format

This sets what OHD writes into Darkroom Pro's **OrderLastName** field. That field is usually what you see in Darkroom Pro's order list.

| Option | Example |
|---|---|
| **{OrderRef} - {LastName}** (default) | PXDEMO-AB12CD - Smith |
| **Customer Last Name only** | Smith |
| **{LabCode}-{OrderRef} - {LastName}** | (website code)-PXDEMO-AB12CD - Smith |

### Photo Lines

These are optional extra lines written for every image, usually for back-print text on the reverse of the photo. You can have up to 2.

* The left box is the Darkroom Pro field name. It must match your Darkroom Pro setup exactly, for example **Photo.First Name**.
* The right box is what OHD writes into that field. You can type text and use tokens.
* A new controller starts with two lines already filled in: **Photo.First Name** = **{filename}** and **Photo.Last Name** = **{lastName}**.
* Click a token under **Available tokens — click to copy:** to copy it, then paste it into the box.

| Token | What it prints |
|---|---|
| **{customerName}** | The customer's full name |
| **{firstName}** | The customer's first name |
| **{lastName}** | The rest of the customer's name |
| **{orderNumber}** | The order number |
| **{jobName}** | The job number, for example PXDEMO-AB12CD-1 (on a reprint, PXDEMO-AB12CD-1-r1) |
| **{jobId}** | The OrderHub job ID |
| **{filename}** | The image's file name |
| **{originalFilename}** | The name of the file the customer uploaded (blank if there isn't one) |

![Backprinting with tokens](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/a58bd777-8c63-4991-aa63-982ee14d34dc.png)

### Size Translations

Map an exact product code to the size string Darkroom Pro expects.

1. Click **+ Add Size**.
2. In **Product Code**, type the product code exactly (for example **0406-cut-print**). Capitals don't matter, but it must be the whole code.
3. In **Size**, type the size name exactly as it is in Darkroom Pro (for example **4x6**).

* Note: a size picked by hand on a job, in **Assign Channel** or with Crop to Size in Job Review, always wins over this table.

### Media Translations

Specify which job option carries the paper type, and translate its values.

1. In **Paper Type Option Key**, type the name of the product option that holds the paper choice, for example **finish-options**.
2. Click **+ Add Media Translation**.
3. In **Option value**, type the customer's choice (for example **lustre**).
4. In **Darkroom value**, type the paper name exactly as it is in Darkroom Pro (for example **Lustre 1**).

* Note: if you add Media Translations, the **Paper Type Option Key** is required. Otherwise the controller won't save.
* Note: a job whose paper doesn't match any row can't be sent. It shows **Assign** so you can pick the size and paper by hand.

![Size and Media](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/04e5c209-68f1-44c6-9406-c15b4237a9f5.png)

### Auto Print — Send jobs to print automatically

When ticked, jobs for this controller are sent to Darkroom Pro as soon as they're ready. When unticked, OHD doesn't watch for Darkroom Pro taking the order. The job still moves to **In Production** as soon as the file is written, and you complete it in OrderHub once it's printed.

### Check Order Status

When ticked, OHD waits for Darkroom Pro to take each order:

* **Taken:** once Darkroom Pro moves the order's .txt file out of the Output Path, the job stays **In Production** and shows **Accepted by Darkroom Pro**. Darkroom Pro taking the file doesn't mean the prints are finished. So OHD doesn't complete the job; you complete it in OrderHub as usual, and OHD follows.
* **Rejected:** if Darkroom Pro rejects the order, the job goes to error with **Darkroom Pro rejected this order:** followed by the reason.
* **Not picked up:** if Darkroom Pro hasn't taken the file after 15 minutes, a warning appears under **In Production**: "Darkroom Pro hasn't picked this order up after 15 minutes — check Darkroom Pro is running and watching the Output Path." It clears once Darkroom Pro takes the file.

When unticked, the job is marked completed in OrderHub as soon as the file is written.

* Note: OHD only checks while its service is running. That needs at least one of these switched on:
  * **Settings → Downloads → Download new orders automatically**;
  * **Settings → Film Scans → Enable Film Scans**;
  * **Settings → File Uploads → Enable File Uploads**;
  * **Settings → Order XML → Enable Order XML Hot Folders**.
  If the tray icon shows **Service: OFF**, jobs stay as they are until the service is started again.
* Note: reprints aren't followed, and neither are jobs sent before this version of OHD.

### Maximum prints per job (optional)

Splits a large job into smaller Darkroom Pro orders so one big job doesn't hold up the printer. Copies of the same photo are always kept together. Leave blank for no limit.

**Send batches automatically**: Off: a large job waits for you to check it, then **Process** splits and sends it. On: large jobs don't wait — with Auto Print on, they're split and sent straight away.

* Note: this box is greyed out until you set a maximum.

### Combine jobs from the same order

When one order has several jobs for this printer (for example 6x4s and 5x7s), send them to Darkroom Pro as one order instead of one per job. This applies to automatic sending; a job sent by hand with **Process** goes on its own.

**Maximum wait for the rest of the order (minutes)**: Safety net only. OHD normally sends the combined order as soon as all its jobs are ready. If one job is held up, OHD stops waiting after this many minutes and sends each ready job as its own Darkroom Pro order — they are not combined. The held-up job stays held. Leave blank for 30 minutes.

## Image Borders: Page Padding

Some sizes print best on a slightly larger page with white space on one side. For example, a 5x7 printed as a 6x7 page with a 1-inch white strip on the right. The print then needs only one cut to trim it, and every print of that size gets its white space on the same side.

Page padding does this automatically in OHD, so nothing needs setting up in your image files.

![Page Padding](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/f1267a32-9ba9-41bf-af54-913001798730.png)

### Setting it up

1. Open the controller in **Settings → Routing → Order Controllers** and click **Edit**.
2. Under **Page padding**, click **+ Add Page Padding**.
3. In **When Size is**, type the size that should be padded, for example **5x7**.
4. In **Send as**, type the page size to print on, for example **6x7**.
5. In **White space**, choose **Left**, **Right**, **Top** or **Bottom**.
6. Click **Save Controller**.

| When Size is | Send as | White space |
|---|---|---|
| 5x7 | 6x7 | Right |
| 11x14 | 12x14 | Right |

Rules for each row:

* Sizes are width x height in inches.
* **Send as** must be bigger in one direction only, and the same in the other. 5x7 to 6x7 is fine; 5x7 to 6x8 isn't.
* If the page is wider, the white space must be **Left** or **Right**. If it's taller, it must be **Top** or **Bottom**.
* Each size can only be listed once.
* Note: **When Size is** is the Darkroom Pro size name, the one your **Size Translations** produce, not the product code.
* Note: **Send as** is the size OHD sends to Darkroom Pro. That size (for example **6x7**) must exist in Darkroom Pro.

### What OHD does to each image

1. If the image is turned the other way to the print size (a landscape image for a portrait 5x7), OHD turns it a quarter-turn clockwise so it's upright. This keeps the white strip on the same side for every print.
2. OHD checks the image's shape. If it's within 2% of the print size, OHD trims the tiny difference evenly from the edges. If it's further out, OHD won't pad it (see below).
3. OHD places the image on the larger white page, with all the white space on the side you chose. The image is not resized, so there's no loss of detail.
4. OHD saves the page as a top-quality JPEG (quality 100) with the image's colour profile kept, in the job's **cache** folder, and sends that to Darkroom Pro.

Your original image is never changed. Reprints are padded the same way.

![Darkroom Pro Paper](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/e587194e-1da5-4e62-9231-48aa9555c4cb.png)

### When OHD refuses to pad an image

If any image in the job can't be padded, OHD sends nothing for that job and marks it as an error. You'll see a message starting **Darkroom Pro page padding refused**, followed by the reason:

| Reason shown | What to do |
|---|---|
| Image shape doesn't match 5x7; page padding refused — crop it to size in Job Review and resend. | Crop the image to size in Job Review, then send again |
| The image is CMYK; page padding refused — save it as RGB and resend. | Save the image as RGB and send again |
| Image dimensions could not be read; page padding refused. | The file may be damaged. Replace it and send again |
| … would both be padded to …; page padding refused — rename one of them and resend. | Two images in the job have the same name. Rename one and send again |

* Note: if the job was part of a combined order, every job in that order is held back, so nothing prints until the problem is fixed.

---

## Using a Second Printer

If Darkroom Pro drives more than one printer, OHD can send work to either one. You don't need to change anything in Darkroom Pro.

### How Darkroom Pro picks the printer

In Darkroom Pro, each paper roll is loaded by width (4 inch, 5 inch, 6 inch and so on), and each print size is given to the roll width it prints on. Each printer's paper also has its own name. So the lustre paper on your first printer might be called **Lustre 1**, and on your second printer **Lustre 2**.

Darkroom Pro sends each order to the printer that has the paper named in the instruction file.

![Darkroom Pro Paper](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/82d89afe-1e68-42d4-8281-46ad6b3944e4.png)

### Always printing a paper on the second printer

If a paper is only loaded on your second printer, you don't need a second controller. In your normal controller's **Media Translations**, set that paper's **Darkroom value** to the second printer's paper name, for example **metallic** to **Metallic 2**. Every job on that paper then goes to the second printer.

### Moving a job to the second printer

Use this when your main printer is busy and you want to move a job onto the second one. You'll need a second Darkroom Pro controller in OHD that sends the second printer's paper names.

**Setting up the second controller:**

1. Set up your first controller as normal, for example **Darkroom – Printer 1**, with its **Media Translations** sending **lustre** as **Lustre 1**. This is your default controller: your products reach it through **Process Routing** and **Channel Mappings** in **Settings → Routing**.
2. On that controller's card, click **Duplicate**. The **Add Controller** window opens with a copy of every setting, named **Darkroom – Printer 1 (copy)**.
3. In **Name**, rename it, for example **Darkroom – Printer 2**.
4. Under **Media Translations**, change each **Darkroom value** to the second printer's paper name, for example **Lustre 1** to **Lustre 2**.
5. Leave the **Output Path** the same. Both controllers write into the same Darkroom Pro Command folder.
6. Click **Save Controller**.

* Note: **Duplicate** doesn't copy **Process Routing** or **Channel Mappings**. Leave it that way, so new jobs always go to your first printer and the second controller is only used when you choose it.
* Note: the second controller keeps its own Size Translations, Photo Lines and Page padding. If you change these on the first controller, change them on the second one too.

**Moving a job:**

1. In Darkroom Pro, cancel the order on the first printer.
2. In OHD, open the job in **Job Review** and select the images to print.
3. In the middle of the top bar is the reprint button, for example **Send 3 Images for Reprint**. Click the **▾** on its right. Under **Reprint to…**, choose **Darkroom – Printer 2**. The job's usual controller is marked **(default)**.
   * Note: clicking the button text itself sends to the default controller. Always use the **▾** to reach the second printer.
4. OHD shows **✓ (job)-r1 sent to Darkroom – Printer 2**.

The reprint goes to Darkroom Pro as a new order with **-r1** on the end of its number, carrying the second printer's paper name, so Darkroom Pro prints it on the second printer. This works even if the paper was picked by hand on the original job.

![Reprint Options](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/211825f1-03cb-493d-aa7a-f08d3740b95e.png)

* Note: the **▾** only appears when more than one controller can print the job. If **Darkroom – Printer 2** isn't listed, check that it has a **Size Translation** for the job's product code and a **Media Translation** for its paper.
* Note: if the send fails, OHD shows the error with a **Retry Send** button, which resends to the controller you chose.
* Note: **Apply & Send Reprint** (in the crop editor, under **Crop to Size → ✂ Crop Image**) sends just that image to the default controller. To reach the second printer, apply the crop with **Apply Crop**, then use the **▾** menu.
* Note: Crop to Size in Job Review also lists the second controller's sizes, shown as **(size) — Darkroom – Printer 2**.

---

## Good to Know

* Sizes and paper names must match Darkroom Pro exactly. Most "nothing printed" problems are a spelling difference.
* A size or paper picked by hand on a job wins over the translation tables. The exception is choosing a different controller under **Reprint to…**, where that controller's paper names are always used.
* Reprints are never combined with other jobs and never split into batches.
* Padded copies are kept in each job's **cache** folder. Your original images are never changed.
* Changes to a controller apply to the next job sent. Jobs already in Darkroom Pro aren't affected.
